subject: Recap & prompt harvest: TitanLaw model recommendations and next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Greer <alex.greer@titanlaw.com>, Jamila Ortiz <jamila@titanlaw.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: prompt harvest template & proposed model candidates

Alex / Jamila — great conversation earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + asks so we can move to an eval run next week: 

Summary of call (short):
- Goal: automate first-pass contract triage + clause extraction and provide safe paraphrase suggestions to lawyers.
- Volume: ~20k documents/month (mix of NDAs, MSAs, SOWs).
- Data sensitivity: client names and account numbers must be redacted before leaving TitanLaw environment.
- Success metrics discussed: extraction F1 > 0.85 on key clause types; hallucination rate < 2% for paraphrases; latency target < 800ms p95.

Asks / next steps:
1) Prompt set: please populate the attached "titanlaw-prompt-request-template.csv" with 10–20 representative prompts and edge cases (we included columns for input type, expected output, redaction rules).
2) Sample docs: upload 50 representative documents to the secure upload link we'll send (PII redaction rule examples are helpful).
3) Redaction guidance: confirm which fields must always be redacted (client legal entity, account numbers, DOB). If redaction is not possible for the sample set, flag examples in the CSV.
4) Workshop: propose a 60-min technical workshop next week to walk through the prompt set and initial eval plan (Marissa will lead the workshop). Options: Tue 4/13 or Wed 4/14 10–12 PT.

Initial model candidates (for evaluation):
- Redwood-3.0-codex-like (higher quality / higher cost) — recommended for paraphrase + clause synthesis tests.
- Redwood-2.1-optimized (good latency/cost tradeoff) — candidate for extraction + triage.
- Redwood-quantized-2-small (low-cost baseline) — good to establish cost floor; expect precision tradeoffs.

I've attached the CSV template to make prompt collection quick. If you prefer, send a handful of live prompts inline and we'll transcribe them.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
https://redwood.ai
From: Alex Greer <alex.greer@titanlaw.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamila Ortiz <jamila@titanlaw.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt harvest template & proposed model candidates

Neha — thanks, appreciated. Attaching our initial prompt set as requested ("titanlaw-prompt-examples.csv") and a short internal note on redaction. Highlights / notes: 

- Attached includes 12 prompts across three buckets: clause extraction, clause classification, paraphrase & plain-English summary.
- Edge cases called out in column "edge_case": nested indemnity, ambiguous effective dates, cross-referenced attachments.
- Redaction: we need FULL redaction of client legal entity names and financial account numbers. Party initials are okay to keep. Client prefer HMAC-style tokenization for production, but for evaluation we can provide redacted examples (see attached redaction_note.txt).
- Quick sample prompt (pasted inline):

  Prompt #7 (paraphrase): 
  "Rewrite the following confidentiality clause in plain English for a non-legal audience, preserving obligations and exceptions.
  Input: 'The Receiving Party shall not disclose Confidential Information except as expressly permitted herein...'"

- We can make the secure upload available; Jamila will coordinate with your SRE.

Two small asks from our side:
1) Can you indicate the expected token costs for the three candidate models for an average 250-token prompt + 500-token response?
2) If Redwood runs the benchmark, can we get a short pre-release summary before sharing internally?

Thanks, Alex

--
Alex Greer
Director of Legal Technology, TitanLaw
alex.greer@titanlaw.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Greer <alex.greer@titanlaw.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt harvest template & proposed model candidates

Alex — perfect, got the CSV and the redaction note. Quick answers and next steps below.

Token cost estimates (ballpark, per 250-token prompt + 500-token response):
- Redwood-3.0-codex-like: ~ $0.12 per eval (higher accuracy, higher cost).
- Redwood-2.1-optimized: ~ $0.045 per eval (good balance).
- Redwood-quantized-2-small: ~ $0.011 per eval (low-cost baseline, expect drop in paraphrase fidelity).

Benchmark / pre-release summary: yes — we will run the eval on your supplied prompt set and return a short executive summary PDF before you circulate internally. That preview will include the per-model metrics (F1, precision/recall for extraction, hallucination flags, latency p95).

Proposed evaluation plan (short):
1) Secure upload: Jamila to share S3 link or SharePoint -> we will provide minimal instructions and a manifest.
2) Redwood runs baseline evals on the three candidate variants across the 12 prompts + 50 sample docs.
3) We return a 1-page exec summary (benchmark-results-preview.pdf) and a deeper technical report if you want more detail.
4) If results look good, plan a 2-week pilot with dedicated routing and prefix caching to meet latency/cost targets.

Workshop: Marissa and I can run a 60-min workshop on Tue 4/13 at 11:00 AM PT — will send a calendar invite if that works. Marissa will demo how we capture edge cases in the eval harness and how we instrument hallucination checks.

Attachments: I attached a short preview of the benchmark template ("benchmark-results-preview.pdf") to show the format of the executive summary.

Logging and quality regression: one note — Marissa will go over our regression hooks in the workshop, but briefly: we recommend pinning a prompt set of 50 canonical prompts and running nightly regression checks on new model versions. If you have existing in-house test cases, we can integrate them into our alerting.

Next steps (concrete):
- Jamila -> share upload link (today).
- Alex -> confirm workshop time (proposed Tue 4/13 11:00 AM PT).
- We -> run baseline eval and return preview by EOD Thu 4/15.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Alex Greer <alex.greer@titanlaw.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt harvest template & proposed model candidates

Neha / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Tue 4/13 11:00 AM PT works for us. Jamila will send the upload link for the 50 docs by EOD today. Looking forward to the preview.

Alex
